terms.latin: commentāriī periodicī, commentāriōrum periodicōrum m. pl.
terms.comment: Commentārius is classically a notebook or a record (Lewis & Short); periodicus, recurring, is in the elder Pliny. Traupman calls a magazine commentāriī periodicī imāgineī, an illustrated periodical (p. 343), and a journal plain commentāriī periodicī (p. 335); Morgan–Owens also has the singular commentārium periodicum (Egger).

evidence: M-O s.v. magazine, periodical, journal, after Egger
terms.comment: Classically a day-book or diary (Lewis & Short); in modern Latin any periodical, and a newspaper.

sources: Lewis & Short: commentarius · Lewis & Short: periodicus · Lewis & Short: ephemeris
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. magazine, periodical, journal.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 335, 343, 359.
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 56, s.v. rivista.
